detaileddescription.para: Thanks for helping improve Valhalla. This document covers how the code is organised and the conventions that keep the documentation and source consistent. For build and install instructions see README.md; for a map of the runtime components see ARCHITECTURE.md.

sect1.title: Code organisation
sect1.para: New source files under src/ are picked up automatically by CMake's recursive glob (src/*.cpp); there is no manual source list to edit.

listitem.para: C++20. Build with -Wall -Wextra -pedantic; do not introduce new warnings.
Formatting is defined by .clang-format (LLVM-derived, 4-space indent, brace-on-next-line for functions). Run clang-format -i on touched files.
.clang-tidy configures static analysis; address findings in code you touch.
compile_commands.json is generated for clangd; editor configs for VS Code and Zed are included under .vscode/ and .zed/.

sect1.title: Documentation conventions
sect1.para: All public and private declarations are documented with Doxygen /** ... */ blocks so doxygen Doxyfile produces a complete reference. Follow these rules:

listitem.para: Document intent, not syntax. Explain why a lock, branch, or type is needed, not that the line increments a counter.

Complete contracts. Each function documents parameters (@param[in], @param[out], @param[in,out]), return value (@return), side effects, pre/postconditions, exceptions (@throws), and thread-safety or ownership requirements where they are known.
Evidence only. Never invent behaviour, guarantees, or exceptions. If a property cannot be established from the implementation, say so explicitly.
Preserve accurate existing comments. Correct them only when the code provides clear evidence.
Classes carry @class and @brief plus a @details paragraph covering responsibility, lifecycle, ownership and thread-safety.
Members and non-obvious locals get a short comment explaining what they represent and why they exist; do not add comments that merely restate code.
Ownership and concurrency matter. Call out unique_ptr vs shared_ptr, borrowed references, std::move, const correctness, atomic memory ordering, and lock ordering wherever they affect maintenance.

sect2.title: Shell scripts
sect2.para: Shell scripts under scripts/, tools/, docker/, .github/ and the repository root use the same header fields, written as #-prefixed lines immediately after the shebang (@file, @brief, @author, @date), plus # @brief / # @param blocks above each function and # WHY comments for non-obvious commands. Doxygen has no shell parser, so .sh files are not part of the Doxygen INPUT; they are documented in-source and read directly.

build.sh wraps these steps and runs the tests via CTest presets. Tests run without a database (VALHALLA_TEST_NO_DB=true), so they work on any machine. Useful build options: -DENABLE_TESTS=OFF and -DVALHALLA_BUILD_DOCS=OFF.

listitem.para: Open an issue to discuss substantial changes before implementing them.
Keep commits focused; one logical change per pull request.
Add or update Doxygen comments alongside code changes, and update ARCHITECTURE.md when component relationships change.
Run clang-format, build and run the test suite before submitting.
Confirm documentation changes do not alter behaviour; the audit in DOCUMENTATION_AUDIT.md describes how this is verified.
